summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with a history of common variable immunodeficiency, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and recent allogeneic stem cell transplant was admitted with fever and worsening diarrhea. Evaluation confirmed acute gastrointestinal graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) and CMV reactivation. She was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone, transitioned to oral prednisone, and received ganciclovir for CMV, later switched to oral valganciclovir. She required TPN for nutritional support, which was discontinued as her oral intake improved. A CT scan revealed incidental pneumonia, treated with cefepime and azithromycin. Her stoma inflammation was monitored without biopsy, and leg swelling was found not to be due to DVT. She improved clinically, advanced to a Phase V GI diet, and was discharged home on immunosuppressive, antiviral, and supportive therapies with close outpatient follow-up.
